name: Budgeted English Auction Series
summary: Six items are auctioned one per round. Each auction has three simultaneous sealed bidding turns, and players hold private values and separate budgets of 30 coins; the highest total of value won minus price paid wins.

player.meaning: Remaining coins. Winning an item reduces it by the price. Unspent coins are worth nothing at the end.
Sum over won items of (private value minus price paid). It may be negative.
The player's private values for items 1 to 6, in item order. It is a random permutation of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.
This bidding turn's submitted bid, where 0 means pass. It stays sealed until all bids are in.
Whether this turn's bid met the validity rule. An invalid bid counts as a pass.
This round's short talk message. It binds nobody.

game.meaning: Current round, which is also the number of the item on sale (1 to 6).
The seat with top tie-break priority this round: ((round - 1) mod N) + 1.
Seats in this round's tie-break order: first_seat, then increasing seat numbers, wrapping around.
Current highest valid bid this round. 0 means no bid yet.
Seat holding the standing bid. 0 means no leader.
Price paid for the most recently resolved item. 0 if the item went unsold.
A temporary copy of [3,5,7,9,11,13], drawn from at random to deal one player's values.

setup: Seats are numbered 1 to N, where N is the number of players.
Every player gets budget 30 and score 0.

For each player in turn, value_pool is set to [3,5,7,9,11,13]. Six times, one entry is drawn at random from value_pool, appended to that player's values list and removed from value_pool. values[k-1] is that player's private value for item k. Each value is used exactly once, so the values sum to 48.
Each player is sent their own values list. No player sees another's values.
round is set to 1, standing_bid to 0, leader to 0 and last_price to 0.

round.effect: first_seat = ((round - 1) mod N) + 1. priority_order = [first_seat, first_seat+1, ..., N, 1, ..., first_seat-1]. standing_bid = 0. leader = 0. Every player's bid = 0 and bid_valid = false.
Announce: 'Item {round} is on sale. Priority order: {priority_order}. Budgets: {budget of each seat}. Scores: {score of each seat}.'
Each player's message is set to their reply. Once all replies are in, broadcast {"to": "all", "text": "Seat {seat} says: {value}"}. Messages bind nobody.

round.answer: a whole number from 0 to your budget; 0 = pass, otherwise a bid of at least 1
round.effect: Bidding turn 1. Each player's bid = reply. bid_valid = (bid >= 1 and bid <= budget). If any bid_valid: the valid bidder with the highest key = bid * 10 + (N - 1 - ((seat - first_seat) mod N)) becomes leader, and standing_bid = that bid. Otherwise standing_bid = 0 and leader = 0.
Announce 'Standing bid {standing_bid} by seat {leader}' if leader > 0, else 'No bid.'

round.answer: a whole number from 0 to your budget; 0 = pass, otherwise a bid of at least standing_bid + 1
round.effect: Bidding turn 2. Each player's bid = reply. bid_valid = (bid >= standing_bid + 1 and bid >= 1 and bid <= budget). The leader may bid too. If any bid_valid: the valid bidder with the highest key = bid * 10 + (N - 1 - ((seat - first_seat) mod N)) becomes leader, and standing_bid = that bid. Otherwise standing_bid and leader are unchanged.
Announce 'Standing bid {standing_bid} by seat {leader}' if leader > 0, else 'No bid.'

round.answer: a whole number from 0 to your budget; 0 = pass, otherwise a bid of at least standing_bid + 1
round.effect: Bidding turn 3, the same as turn 2: bid_valid = (bid >= standing_bid + 1 and bid >= 1 and bid <= budget). The valid bidder with the highest key becomes leader, and standing_bid = that bid. If there is no valid bid, nothing changes.
Announce 'Final standing bid {standing_bid} by seat {leader}' if leader > 0, else 'No bid; item {round} goes unsold.'

When leader > 0: the leader's budget -= standing_bid, the leader's score += values[round - 1] - standing_bid, and last_price = standing_bid. When leader = 0: last_price = 0 and nobody's budget or score changes.
If leader > 0, announce 'Item {round} sold to seat {leader} for {last_price}.' The winner's value is not announced. Otherwise announce 'Item {round} unsold.'
End the game if round > 6. Otherwise continue with the next round.

ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their score: the total of private values of items won minus prices paid. Unspent budget counts for nothing. The highest score wins. Players level at the top share the win, which stands in for the source's draw.

rules.text: When the game starts, every player has budget 30 and score 0, and a private values list that is a permutation of [3,5,7,9,11,13] summing to 48.
When the game starts, each player's values list is visible only to that player.
In round r, item r is sold, for r from 1 to 6.
In round r with N players, priority starts at seat ((r - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in increasing seat order, wrapping around; with N = 3, round 2's order is 2, 3, 1.
At the start of each round, the item number, priority order, every budget and every score are announced.
Before bidding each round, every player submits one short message simultaneously, and all messages are then shown to everyone.
In bidding turn 1, a bid is valid only if it is at least 1 and at most the bidder's budget; 0 or an invalid bid counts as a pass.
In bidding turn 1, if at least one valid bid is made, the highest valid bid becomes standing_bid and its bidder becomes leader; if none is made, standing_bid = 0 and leader = 0.
In bidding turns 2 and 3, a bid is valid only if it is at least standing_bid + 1 (at least 1 when there is no standing bid) and at most the bidder's budget; otherwise it counts as a pass.
In bidding turns 2 and 3, if any valid bid is made, the highest valid bid becomes standing_bid and its bidder becomes leader; if none is made, standing_bid and leader are unchanged.
When two or more players make the same highest valid bid in a turn, the one earliest in this round's priority order becomes leader; e.g. in round 1 with seats 1 and 3 both bidding 8, seat 1 leads.
The current leader may bid in turns 2 and 3 but need not.
After each bidding turn, the standing bid and leader (or no bid) are announced.
When a round ends with a leader, the leader's budget falls by standing_bid and their score changes by (their value for this item minus standing_bid); e.g. value 7 bought at 10 gives score -3.
When a round ends with a leader, the price is announced but the winner's private value is not.
When a round ends with no leader, the item is unsold and no budget or score changes.
When round 6 is resolved, the game ends.
When the game ends, the player with the highest score wins, unspent budget is worth 0, and players tied at the highest score share the result as a draw.

offers.question: Bidding turn 1
offers.options: Pass (0), or a whole-number bid from 1 to the seat's own budget. A seat with budget 0 may only pass.

offers.question: Bidding turns 2 and 3
offers.who: every seat, including the current leader
offers.options: Pass (0), or a whole-number bid from standing_bid + 1 to the seat's own budget. A seat whose budget is below standing_bid + 1 may only pass. The engine range is 0 to budget, and any entry from 1 to standing_bid is treated as a pass.

choices.why: The designer suggested 3, so it is kept. The minimum is 3 because an auction needs at least two rivals for price competition and for the tie-break rotation to matter. The maximum stays at the source's 5 because larger tables make each seat's bids marginal and the talk long.

choices.what: Kept simultaneous talk as a poll with broadcast
choices.why: The rules require it. Players disagree, since each wants the others to stay out of the items they value most, so non-binding claims about values and intentions are worth reasoning about and doubting.

choices.what: Pass encoded as bid 0, with a bid range of 0 to budget
choices.why: The engine takes whole numbers in a range. Bids above budget cannot be entered, and the source treats them as passes anyway.

choices.what: Tie-break computed as key = bid * 10 + (N - 1 - ((seat - first_seat) mod N))
choices.why: This gives the priority order arithmetically. The multiplier 10 exceeds N, so the bid always dominates.
The source's 'no standing bid' needs a concrete state value.

choices.what: The six item values are listed as separate parameters item_value_1 to item_value_6
choices.why: Each parameter must be a single number. They are the values dealt to every player, not tied to specific items.

choices.what: Scores remain public, as the source states
choices.why: The source says budgets and scores are public but values are private. A public score change lets observers deduce the winner's value; this is kept faithfully.

With 30 coins against a 48-value set, a thoughtful player plans which items to chase given their own values and the rotating tie-break. They shade bids below value and read rivals' remaining budgets and talk. A thoughtless one overspends early or bids above value.

simplifications.what: An invalid bid in turns 2 and 3 (1 to standing_bid) can still be typed and is treated as a pass
simplifications.why: The engine range cannot have a gap between pass and the minimum raise. The source's own rule says invalid bids count as passes.

simplifications.what: The source's 'draw' is a shared win among the top-scoring players
simplifications.why: The engine has no separate draw outcome. Players level at the top share the win.
